items.headline: Picking the right Copilot for the job: Tips from our experience at Microsoft
items.summary: Microsoft's internal IT team shares actionable guidance on choosing the right AI assistant for different work scenarios. The article covers when to use M365 Copilot for business context versus GitHub Copilot for development tasks, explains how custom instructions and memory features reduce prompt editing time, and reveals that voice prompts often capture context more clearly than typing. Microsoft reports organizations save an average of two hours per week per employee when AI assistants are matched to the right tasks.
items.levelshiftAngle: LevelShift deploys both M365 Copilot and GitHub Copilot for clients across Manufacturing and Financial Services verticals — this Microsoft-sourced decision framework helps us coach enterprise teams on tool selection during our AI Discovery & Assessment Workshops. The tip on custom instructions reducing editing time is directly applicable to our Salesforce and Microsoft Dynamics implementation teams. Share this with delivery leads this week as a structured talking point for client workshops.

items.headline: Health system AI adoption surges in 2026 with execs reporting increased ROI: survey
items.summary: More than half of US health systems that quantified AI ROI reported at least 2x returns in 2026, with the average ROI reaching $3.20 per dollar invested within 14 months. Advocate Health System projects that embedding FDA-approved AI models into imaging workflows will benefit 63,000 patients annually through faster diagnoses. Medical coding improvements deliver $5M-$15M in annual revenue capture for a typical 200-bed hospital, while sepsis detection returns $1M-$2M annually. Clinical documentation shows 68% adoption with 62% year-over-year growth.

items.headline: EY cybersecurity report pulled after probe finds 'AI hallucinations'
items.summary: EY Canada withdrew a 44-page cybersecurity report on loyalty systems after GPTZero's investigation revealed fabricated citations and AI-generated hallucinations. Of 27 cited sources, 16 were either fabricated, misattributed, or linked to broken URLs, including fake references to Forbes, McKinsey, Gartner, and WIRED. EY confirmed the report was not client work but stated they take content accuracy seriously. The incident highlights governance failures even at established consulting firms when AI-generated content lacks human verification.

items.headline: EU AI Act transparency rules come into effect in August 2026
items.summary: The EU AI Act's transparency requirements become enforceable on August 2, 2026, with compliance required for high-risk AI systems used in employment, credit decisions, education, and law enforcement. Additional rules for biometrics, critical infrastructure, and migration systems apply from December 2027. Penalties reach 7% of global revenue for prohibited AI violations and 3% for high-risk non-compliance. A political agreement on amendments was reached May 7, 2026, clarifying timelines and risk categories.
